about.title: Loomis Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Loomis is a small town, but its roads carry a lot of traffic, and the public record shows it: 17 injury collisions and 26 injured people in the most recent full year, with one traffic death. Corridors like Sierra College Boulevard, Taylor Road, Horseshoe Bar Road, and Laird Road see the most reported crashes, and Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to be when collisions cluster. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days right after matter. Placer County roads are patrolled by CHP and local law enforcement, and insurance adjusters move fast to lock in a version of events that favors them. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured Loomis residents and visitors with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at what happened, explain your options, and handle communication with insurers on your behalf.
about.ctaText: Get connected with a Loomis-area injury attorney — free, no obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Again

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash to file a personal injury claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like Placer County or Loomis roadway maintenance — may be involved. Waiting to sort this out can quietly cost you your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Shared Blame Doesn't End Your Case
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for a crash on Taylor Road or Horseshoe Bar Road, you may still recover a share of damages. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't unfairly pinned on you before you've had a chance to respond.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Full Story Matters
items.desc: California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so documenting how an injury has actually affected your life in Loomis — work, family, daily routine — carries real weight. It's also why giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney is rarely a good idea.

items.question: I was in a crash on Sierra College Boulevard. Should I talk to the other insurance company first?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can talk to the insurer on your behalf so you don't have to navigate it alone.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Loomis car accident?
items.answer: In California, you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a public road authority, may share responsibility, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth getting guidance early rather than waiting.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility for the crash. Your potential recovery is simply adjusted based on your percentage of fault, rather than being barred entirely.
